text:
Elena: Hit an odd installer edge on a shared lab box. After running the macOS pkg, redwoodctl created ~/.redwood/profiles.json but the SSO helper (launch agent) can't read it -> local serve 403s.
Marcus: What do perms look like?
Elena: `-rw------- 1 elena staff 245 Apr 10 09:03 ~/.redwood/profiles.json` but the launch agent runs as a different launchd session that needs group read. Our users historically set a permissive umask (002) but this machine had umask 077.
Dina: Oh interesting. The installer assumes default umask and doesn't explicitly set file modes. So on strict umask installs the file ends up too restrictive for multi-session helpers.
Marcus: Workaround?
Elena: `chmod 640 ~/.redwood/profiles.json && chgrp staff ~/.redwood/profiles.json` fixed it for me. Restarted the agent with `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.redwood.auth` and local serve started serving requests.
Dina: Two follow-ups: (1) installer should explicitly set secure but usable modes (e.g., 0640) when creating per-user files so helpers in the same user group can read them; (2) add a `redwoodctl fix-perms` command that validates and repairs common perms/ownership problems.
Marcus: Also we should document umask caveats for sysadmins who bake images. Many CI/VM images set umask 077 for security and then processes that expect group access break.
elena: I'll open an issue and attach the minimal repro steps + a brief installer patch suggestion.
infra-bot: Issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/5765 — "installer: ensure per-user config files set 0640 perms and support redwoodctl fix-perms" (labels: devex, security)
Dina: Small UX note: when redwoodctl falls back to ephemeral session due to unreadable profiles, log a WARNING linking to docs and the new fix-perms command. Silent fallbacks are a big source of confusion.
Marcus: Agreed. I'll take the installer PR; Dina can own the fix-perms CLI work.
Elena: Thanks everyone — saved me a bunch of time.
